newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares end mixed after Friday's gains.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares end mixed after Friday's gains.

text.p: Leading Russian shares ended mixed on low volume, with many stocks easing after a strong rise last Friday, and traders said the outlook was uncertain now that foreign orders from Friday had been met.
The RTS index of 24 shares rose 1.05 percent to 173.53 on volume of $7.87 million, down from $18.17 million last Friday.

Traders said last week's 3.41 percent rise of the RTS index on Friday was mostly due to Western orders on news of progress towards rescheduling Russia's commercial bank debt and confirmation it planned to issue Eurobonds this year.
"It didn't look like we had any action from London or New York today, so it was fairly quiet," said Nick Mokhoff of Alliance-Menatep.
He said he did not expect great changes later this week. "Tomorrow -- pretty much the same thing. I do not anticipate a huge rise."
Other traders said that the stock market in Russia was still depressed by concerns about President Boris Yeltsin's health, and Friday's rise was more surprising than Monday's fall.
"I do not see any reasons for growth... Nothing extraordinary happened today, so I am more inclined to be surprised by Friday's growth," said Andrei Kukk of Rinaco-Plus.
The market has been weakening since Yeltsin announced on September 5 he would undergo a heart operation later this month.
Norilsk Nickel, which says it is in deep financial trouble and may have to lay off staff, fell to $6.70 from $6.98 at Friday's close on the Russian Trading System (RTS).
But retailer GUM, included in the newly expanded RTS index, rose to $19.00 from $18.80, while utility Lenenergo, also included, fell to $0.355 from $0.365.
UES edged down to $0.0787 from $0.0797. Mosenergo slipped to $0.951 from $0.957.
